name: sequential attention replaces the combinational form
why_this_iteration_exists: Iteration 2 rejected the combinational attention form because it consumed 21.3% of the XC7A200T LUT fabric and declared that a sequential form was required. This iteration builds and measures that sequential form.

design.change: one KV slot is scored per cycle instead of all SLOTS in parallel; the combinational depth drops from SLOTS x HEAD_DIM MAC steps to HEAD_DIM MAC steps
design.cache: same bounded quantised KV cache: sign + QUANT_W magnitude bits of an ACT_BITS-wide value

methodology.latency: DERIVED from the cycle count (one slot per cycle); not measured on silicon

head_to_head.latency_cost: 16 cycles per attention pass instead of 1 (at ~150 MHz: ~107 ns instead of ~6.7 ns of combinational depth)

findings.claim: The sequential form needs 362-777 estimated LCs across every configuration measured (0.27%-0.58% of the XC7A200T LUT fabric). The 10% resource cap is no longer binding for any configuration in the sweep.

With the sequential form the per-slot cost is visible: at act=8/quant=8, KV_LEN 8 -> 16 -> 32 gives 362 -> 455 -> 777 LCs and 275 -> 341 -> 471 FFs, i.e. about 9.3 LCs and 6.6 FFs per extra slot. This closes the 'KV_LEN scaling not characterised' gap recorded in iteration 2 (the earlier saturation was a combinational-mux artifact).

In the sequential form the activation/KV width is nearly free: act=8/quant=8 -> 455 LCs, act=6/quant=6 -> 437 LCs, act=4/quant=4 -> 453 LCs at kv_len=16. The bottleneck moved from combinational score logic to the cache registers, so narrowing the width buys nothing.

Iteration 2 accepted act=4/quant=4 because it was the cheapest LOSSLESS configuration under the 10% cap in the combinational form. In the sequential form act=8/quant=8 is just as cheap AND lossless with no quality constraint to satisfy, so the recommendation is now act=8/quant=8.
DSP48E1 = 0 and RAMB = 0 in every sequential configuration. The KV cache is fabric registers; external DRAM reads per token = 0 and KV traffic = 0 bytes/token.

decision: ADOPT the sequential attention form with act_bits=8, quant_w=8
decision_rationale: 455 estimated LCs = 0.34% of the device, so the 10% cap no longer binds and wider KV caches become affordable.
act=8/quant=8 is bit-exact against the full-precision golden (iteration 2 measured 0.000000 mean relative error for this point) with no quality compromise at all.
The cost is latency: 16 cycles per attention pass instead of 1. For an autoregressive workload that is 16x more cycles per token, which must be weighed against the 62x LC saving.
known_limitations: The RTL accumulates the attention output continuously and does not reset it between tokens, so the per-token control sequence (reset, scan, write) is not yet implemented. The resource numbers are valid; the per-token cycle count is an estimate of the scan phase only.
Latency is DERIVED, not measured on silicon.
The per-slot cost is now measured, but with the uniform harness payload the mux trees inside a slot may still collapse; a randomised payload sweep would refine the per-slot figure.
next_iteration: implement the per-token control sequence (reset, scan, write) so the cycle count per token is exact
randomised KV payload sweep to confirm the per-slot cost
measure the sequential form's latency on the board and derive the real tok/s
build the sequential bitstream and close the attention latency gate
